common.accelNoChannelBody: This application ships no channel and runs no proxy. To accelerate, add a prefix-style proxy address of your own; otherwise everything stays on a direct connection.
common.accelPrefixOnlyBody:
A custom channel **allows prefix-style proxies only** (such as the GHproxy project): the complete original link is appended after the proxy prefix.

Proxy forms that need to rewrite request headers, rewrite URL paths, or implement their own authentication logic are not supported.

**Note**: a prefix-style proxy may **lack some proxy endpoints**. If some feature misbehaves or network loading fails, you can try switching to another custom channel or turning acceleration off.
common.accelSelfProvided: Channels are yours to provide: this app bundles none, recommends none, and hosts none.
common.accelThirdPartyBody:
1. What this is
This is the notice for a **custom acceleration channel**. The channel address is **added by you**, and its operator is **not** the developer of this application.

**This application ships no acceleration channel of its own and provides no proxy service.** If you add no channel, there is no acceleration.

2. Prefix-style proxies only
This application **supports prefix-style proxies only** (for example the GHproxy project): the complete original link is appended after the proxy prefix, as in `https://your-proxy/original-full-link`.

Proxy forms that need to rewrite request headers, rewrite URL paths, or implement their own authentication logic are **not supported**.

3. Capabilities may be incomplete (please be aware)
1. A prefix-style proxy may **lack some endpoints**, so certain kinds of resources may be unavailable through it.
2. If some features misbehave or network loading fails, this application will **not silently fall back to a direct connection** — it reports the failure as it is. That is how you can tell whether traffic really went through the channel. If you want a direct connection, turn the main switch off.
3. This application **does not guarantee** the availability, speed, or completeness of any custom channel.

4. Responsibility
1. The channel's operator, availability, bandwidth, stability, content integrity, and security are **the third party's responsibility**; this application gives no warranty of any kind.
2. Once enabled, some download requests (including the target download address) will be sent to that third-party server. Please satisfy yourself that you trust that provider, and assess the privacy, data, and compliance risks on your own.
3. This application compares the SHA-256 digest provided by GitHub where one is available; but if the third party returns a file that does not match, or the resource has no digest, this application **cannot guarantee it was not substituted**.
4. This application accepts no liability for download failures, data corruption, tampered content, privacy leaks, extra charges, or any direct or indirect loss arising from use of that third-party service.
5. You are responsible for checking and complying with the laws and internal policies of your country/region and organisation regarding network access and data transmission.

5. Token protection
To avoid handing your GitHub token to a third party, this application first exchanges it **locally on your device** for a temporary signed address valid for about 30 minutes and suitable for a single file, and hands that address to the channel. Within that validity window the channel could technically take that file itself, and may log the address.

6. Scope and termination
1. This notice is shown from the moment you tick to accept. You may remove the channel or turn the main switch off at any time to stop using it.
2. From the moment you stop, this application sends no further requests to that channel.

onboarding.licenseBody:
§ 1. Open-source licence
This project (OhGithubLost, "OGL") is released under the Apache License 2.0 (Apache-2.0). The full text is in the LICENSE file at the repository root. Under sections 7 and 8 of that licence, the application is provided without warranty of any kind.

§ 2. What this statement covers (read this first)
· This statement covers the application itself only — the software the user installed and runs.
· It does not cover any acceleration channel; channels are added by the user, and each has its own separate agreement, to be read and accepted individually.
· In other words: as long as the user enables no acceleration channel, this statement is the complete privacy arrangement between the user and the application.

§ 3. The application collects nothing
· The application itself does not collect, store or upload any personal data, including but not limited to: usage statistics, crash reports, device identifiers, location, contacts or photo-library contents.
· The application contains no telemetry, analytics, advertising or profiling components, and no third-party tracking SDK.
· The application requests no permission unrelated to its functions; every capability requested, and its purpose, is explained item by item on first launch.

§ 4. Where data resides
· All data the application produces (cache, drafts, downloaded files, logs) exists only on the user's device. Uninstalling removes it.
· The user's GitHub access token is kept only in the device's secure storage (Android Keystore / iOS Keychain / desktop key service). It is always masked in the interface and in logs, and removed from the device on sign-out.
· The developer operates no server that receives user data; there is therefore no "corresponding data on the developer's servers".

§ 5. Network requests
· With acceleration off, the application's network requests go only to official GitHub API and asset domains (api.github.com, github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com and similar).
· Once an acceleration channel is enabled, some download requests traverse that channel; such requests are within the channel's agreement and outside this statement.
· The application verifies the SHA-256 digest of downloaded content where available. When no digest is available, the content is honestly labelled "not verified" — never falsely claimed as verified.

§ 6. Exception: the optional Web feature (important)
· The application additionally offers an optional Web (browser) build. It is off by default and is not within the scope of this statement.
· The Web build runs inside a browser and necessarily depends on the browser, the site host and network intermediaries. Those parties may technically be capable of logging access timestamps, IP addresses, User-Agent strings and similar information. The application cannot make a "no data collection" guarantee on their behalf.
· The exception in this section applies only if the user actively enables that optional Web feature. As long as it remains off (the default), Section 3 applies in full.

§ 7. Children's privacy
This application is not directed at children under 13 years of age. Because the application itself collects no personal information at all, should the user believe the developer holds anything relating to a child, the user is requested to contact the developer as set out in Section 13; the developer will verify and delete it promptly upon confirmation.

§ 8. Security
The application protects user credentials following common practice: the token is held by the operating system's secure storage and is never written in plaintext by the application; the interface and logs are always masked. Note, however, that no storage method can be guaranteed absolutely secure — the security of the user's own device (screen lock, system updates) remains the first line of defence.

§ 9. Security-incident notice
The application itself collects no data, so the scenario of "data leaking through the application itself" does not exist. Should the user identify a security issue relating to this application, the user is requested to notify the developer as set out in Section 13; the developer will remedy it as soon as possible after verification, and will disclose it in the version notes (without personal-information details).

§ 10. User rights and data deletion
· Because data resides only on the user's device, the user may perform "deletion" at any time themselves: clear the cache, delete downloaded files, sign out (which removes the local token), or simply uninstall the application.
· The user is also entitled to obtain the complete source code of the application and to audit the actual practices set out above.
· For matters the application cannot perform on the user's behalf, the user may contact the developer as set out in Section 13.

§ 11. Changes and effective date
· Any material change to this statement ships with a release and re-requests the user's consent inside the application (the consent version number being raised accordingly); it never takes effect silently.
· This statement takes effect on the day the user first launches the application; the latest version is the text displayed inside the application.

§ 12. Consent
Continued use of the application is deemed to mean that the user has read, understood and agreed to this statement. If the user does not agree, the user is requested to cease use and to uninstall the application.

§ 13. Contact
This application is an open-source project; questions and requests are to be raised via the repository Issues: https://github.com/OGL-Teams/OhGithubLost/issues
